clue.text: Sensation about the King left him a three-pipe problem?

definitions.note: the clue phrase stands for a person, the detective who called a puzzling case a three-pipe problem

indicators.note: the word about here means going round, so the shock wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a sensation can be a shock
ER is Latin rex's abbreviation, used for a king or queen

explanation.surface: A startling event concerning the monarch left someone with a baffling puzzle to smoke over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the 'him' who was left the problem: Conan Doyle's detective called a hard case 'quite a three-pipe problem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's fictional detective smoked three pipes over one especially baffling case in The Red-Headed League.

clue.text: Initial letters for a director?

parts.note: to initial a document is to sign it
letters delivered are the post or mail

explanation.surface: Abbreviation of a film director's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial' reads as an adjective; it is the verb, to sign. A director here is anything that directs.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside post with pointing arms guides travellers, so it directs them on their way.

clue.text: To me a lion rampant is excitable

indicators.note: rampant, rearing up wildly, signals the letters of to me a lion run riot

explanation.surface: A heraldic lion rearing up seems highly strung to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily moved by feelings: an excitable person is quick to show passion.

clue.text: Year of reflected glory

parts.note: a calendar year counted by the moon, whose light is only sunlight reflected

explanation.surface: A year spent basking in someone else's success.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the moon, which shines with borrowed sunlight; a calendar based on it gives a moon-month year.

clue.text: Dual transport available so keep going

parts.note: two forms of transport: a car and RY, the abbreviation for railway
two forms of transport: a car and RY, the abbreviation for railway
on means available, as in a dish being on

explanation.surface: Two kinds of vehicle are there, so continue the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dual transport' gives two pieces, CAR and RY (railway).
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is a phrasal verb meaning continue or persist.

clue.text: Sound of bells in Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: Bells ringing somewhere in a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinkling metallic ring is what small bells make, and Alfred of that surname is the strolling actor rogue in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Liquid courage on writer's desk

definitions.note: a phrase describing an object found there, standing for the noun

parts.note: ink is a liquid
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Drink-fuelled bravery sitting on an author's table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid courage' suggests alcohol; it splits into two pieces. Bottle is everyday British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel of writing fluid traditionally sat beside a pen on the desk.

clue.text: One who writes for another — a light-hearted entertainer

explanation.surface: A ghost-writer who is also a cheerful performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden author writes books under another's name, and a spirit, insubstantial at heart, entertains by haunting.

clue.text: Head off criticism for guarantee

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: censure is criticism

explanation.surface: Forestall complaints to secure an assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'prevent'; it removes the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain or secure something, the verb sense of guarantee.

clue.text: Like a chap?

explanation.surface: Resembling a man.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means of the same kind, a match; as a noun it is a man or companion.

clue.text: Adult, so formal dress is about right

indicators.note: is about means one piece goes round the other here

parts.note: a gown is a formal dress

explanation.surface: Being grown-up, the formal frock is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts R inside GOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully developed, mature: an adult is a person who has finished developing.

clue.text: Keen frost can make these difficult to tie

indicators.note: can make tells us the letters of keen frost are made into something new

explanation.surface: Bitter cold weather stiffens the fingers so that sailors' bindings are hard to fasten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges KEEN FROST.
explanation.definitionFit: The square knot used by sailors to tie two rope ends, here in a frosty scene where fingers struggle with it.

clue.text: Two grand acquired in a deal perhaps

definitions.note: describes a card combination one might be dealt

parts.note: two of a kind make a pair
grand can mean regal or royal

explanation.surface: Two thousand pounds gained in a business transaction, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds; it is the adjective. A pair royal is three cards of the same rank, scored in cribbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Three matching cards in cribbage or similar games, which a player may receive from the dealer.

clue.text: Ring a long way from being gold

definitions.text: a long way from being gold

explanation.surface: Jewellery that is far from being made of precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery target the outermost band is furthest from the gold bullseye at the centre.

clue.text: Star getting blue in the evening

parts.note: the sun is a star
blue means sad, down

explanation.surface: A celebrity becoming melancholy as night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: The time the sun sets, close of day, is when evening begins.

clue.text: Deter boys swimming on the sea bottom

definitions.note: describes where the place lies, standing for the noun

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of deter boys moving about

explanation.surface: Discourage lads from going for a dip over the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges DETER BOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish breeding ground lies on the seabed in shallow coastal water.

clue.text: Power the French show in fencing

parts.note: a watt is a unit of power
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Electric power and a French team performing at a sword-fighting tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests swordplay; it means a barrier of woven sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Interwoven rods and twigs, an old material for hurdles and enclosures.

clue.text: It has a bearing on East or West's lead

definitions.text: It has a bearing on East or West's lead

parts.words: It has a bearing on East or West's lead
parts.note: a position measured east or west of Greenwich, so it bears on how far east or west something is

explanation.surface: At the bridge table, something affects East or West's opening card.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge surface (East and West as players, a lead) hides a map reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A coordinate giving angular distance east or west of the Greenwich meridian.

clue.text: What they may do to an actor misusing most of petty cash

definitions.text: What they may do to an actor

indicators.note: misusing means the letters are put to wrong use, rearranged
most of means the last letter of petty cash is dropped

explanation.surface: How a company might treat a performer caught misusing the office float.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops H from PETTY CASH; 'misusing' rearranges the rest, PETTYCAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors may cast a performer repeatedly in the same kind of role.

clue.text: Elegant girl to cry heart out about

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes round the other piece
heart out means the middle letter of cry is removed

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman is about to sob her heart out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart out' strips the middle letter, leaving CY, and 'about' wraps that round the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and sophisticated: something with class is elegant.

clue.text: Expression of delight in light opera

explanation.surface: Joy shown in a Gilbert and Sullivan show.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of relish at tasty food, and the heroine of The Mikado by Gilbert and Sullivan.

clue.text: Find a spare wheel somewhere in London?

explanation.surface: Look for a replacement tyre in some part of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for a spare car wheel, named after a firm in Llanelli, and also an East London district.

clue.text: Under search, young chap rose in outrage

indicators.note: Under places the reversed piece below the search word in this down entry

parts.note: to scan is to search

indicators.note: rose, in a down clue, means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young chap

explanation.surface: Being investigated, a young man rose up in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns LAD upward to DAL, and 'Under' puts it below SCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Public disgrace or shock at wrongdoing, i.e. a public furore.

clue.text: Looked underneath forward part of cutter

indicators.note: underneath places the looking word below the front part in this down entry

parts.note: the bow is the front of a boat
saw means looked

explanation.surface: Glanced below the front of a small sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a boat, matching 'forward part'; it is a tool that cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw with a narrow blade held in a curved frame, a tool used for cutting.

clue.text: Where to get a tip at the right moment

explanation.surface: Where to receive a gratuity just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiard stick's end has a leather tip, and an actor's prompt line marks when to come in, so 'timely' fits.

clue.text: Many adore spice

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
to love is to adore

explanation.surface: Lots of people adore a seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried flower bud used as an aromatic seasoning.

clue.text: When a mile out in the interim results

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of when a mile are put out of order

explanation.surface: Results arrive when a runner is a mile away, during the waiting period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WHEN A MILE; 'results' closes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile is an adverb meaning during the time between, just like 'for now' or 'in the interval'.

clue.text: Happened to be with Lawrence in the desert

parts.note: was means happened to be
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials

explanation.surface: Was with Lawrence of Arabia in the Arabian sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren, uninhabited land, a wilderness or desert.

clue.text: South, no! West a jump bid — cut off?

parts.note: a bound is a leap or jump

explanation.surface: A bridge table exclamation: South refuses as West makes a jump bid.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge surface (players named South and West, a jump bid) hides the charade; 'bid' just completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to leave or be reached because snow blocks the way, i.e. isolated.

clue.text: Bathroom with short member of the family in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the shortened relative goes inside the letters for it

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: an aunt is a family member

explanation.surface: A bathroom with a small relative inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the relative's last letter; 'in' puts the rest inside SA, crossword shorthand for sex appeal, which old slang called 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam bath is a room heated for sweating, so a bath room in two words.

clue.text: Commands area of Kent we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is spoken, not written

parts.note: the Weald is a region of Kent, with 's for 'is' or possession

explanation.surface: A region of the English county is in charge, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; the Weald, its wooded area, said as 'Weald's' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield power or wield authority is to exercise control, so to command.

clue.text: Ships set out and should not be caught?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: the quickest runner escapes capture

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are disordered

explanation.surface: Vessels put to sea and must avoid being captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The swiftest person outruns pursuers, hence is the one unlikely to be caught.
